report.summary: The one failure is a 5 s timeout on `Page.goto('/books')`, and the app's `list_books` deliberately sleeps a random 0–8 s on every page render, so the test fails whenever the sleep exceeds the 5 s fixture timeout. Classify it as flaky rather than a product bug, and fix the cause by removing or bounding the random delay in the app (or giving the UI tests a longer navigation timeout) before rerunning.

causes.title: Random server-side sleep in list_books makes /books slower than the 5 s page timeout
causes.explanation: The test fixture sets the default Playwright timeout to 5000 ms (tests/ui/conftest.py:5-7). BooksPage.open() calls page.goto('/books') (tests/support/pages.py:33-35), which waits for the load event. GET /books renders through render_books(), which calls list_books(), and list_books() starts with time.sleep(random.uniform(0, 8)) (app/main.py:149-150). About 3 of every 8 seconds of possible delay exceed 5 s, so the navigation times out on some runs and passes on others. The failure is the app's timing, not the test's logic, and the same commit can pass on a rerun. The other UI tests that load /books also hit this sleep but happened to finish in time.
evidence: Error: playwright._impl._errors.TimeoutError: Page.goto: Timeout 5000ms exceeded. Call log: navigating to "http://127.0.0.1:53126/books", waiting until "load"
app/main.py:149-150: def list_books(user_id: int) -> list[dict]: time.sleep(random.uniform(0, 8))
app/main.py:250-256: render_books() calls list_books(user["id"]) for every GET /books
Test failed at tests/ui/test_books_ui.py:23 (BooksPage(logged_in_page).open()), before any assertion on the book row ran
Confidence limited: I did not see the CI timing logs or the workflow file, so I have not confirmed that the sleep was the only slow step in this run. The mechanism is clear from the code.
causes.suggested_fix: Remove the random sleep from list_books in app/main.py, or make it deterministic and well under the timeout if it is meant to simulate latency. If the slow path is intended, give the UI navigation a longer timeout (for example page.goto(..., timeout=15000) or a larger default in tests/ui/conftest.py) and say so in the fixture docstring. Then rerun the UI suite several times to confirm it is stable.
